mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a monetary policy shift toward disinflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and supports higher corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA +1% AND UNRATE < 3.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 1% and UNRATE is below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for six consecutive months signals elevated household savings and reduced consumption propensity, which depresses demand for equities sensitive to consumer spending and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for six consecutive months.
